beats.purpose: Introduce the central mystery of how a smartphone pinpoints its location without broadcasting any signals back to orbit.
beats.visual_intent: A solitary phone on the globe receiving passive radio signals from a constellation of orbiting satellites overhead.

beats.purpose: Establish the core mechanism that distance equals the speed of light multiplied by signal travel time.
beats.visual_intent: A timestamped radio wave leaving a satellite and traveling to a receiver, measuring the elapsed transit delay.

beats.purpose: Explain why one distance measurement only defines a sphere, and why a fourth satellite is required to resolve receiver clock bias.
beats.visual_intent: Three overlapping distance spheres narrowing the location to two points, followed by a fourth sphere locking the exact position and syncing the clock.

beats.purpose: Reveal that high-precision positioning would fail without accounting for relativistic time differences in satellite atomic clocks.
beats.visual_intent: Side-by-side atomic clocks showing orbital clocks ticking slightly faster in weaker gravity than Earth-bound clocks.

beats.purpose: Bring the geometric and relativistic pieces together to show an instantaneous, accurate fix on the surface of Earth.
beats.visual_intent: All four satellite signals locking onto the receiver to illuminate the single true intersection point on the Earth map.

output.rationale: The subject addresses an everyday technological mystery: how a passive handheld receiver computes its exact coordinates from space. The question-led arc naturally establishes the basic mental model of time-of-flight distance measurement, complicates it with the geometric need for four intersecting spheres and receiver clock bias, and reveals the non-intuitive relativistic physics required to achieve accuracy.
output.title: How GPS Pinpoints Your Position on Earth
